turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Doctor. Thanks for seeing me. Basically, what brings me in is that I just can't keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore. 

It doesn't even matter if it's important, my focus just... slips. I do computer support, and lately I'll start tracing a client's network problem, and ten minutes later I'll realize I've reread the exact same log entries three times. And I still don't know what they actually say. It's getting really hard to get my work done.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly states they cannot keep their mind on a task long enough to finish it and describes losing focus repeatedly while trying to read work logs.

turns.doctor_question: How long has this difficulty concentrating been going on? Did it start suddenly, or has it been something you've always struggled with?
turns.patient_response: Well, the really serious trouble started about a year and ten months ago. I was fired from my old job back then. When that happened, I lost all the systems and routines I had built up over the years that used to keep me on track. Ever since then, without those structures in place, it's just been a constant struggle.

turns.doctor_question: Looking back to your childhood and teenage years, before you lost your job—did you have similar trouble concentrating or staying focused on tasks, or is this difficulty with attention something that's really new for you in the past couple of years?

And the funny part is, I'd lose it even when I had actually done it. So, yeah, the trouble focusing and staying on track has always been there, it's just gotten a lot harder to manage lately.
